newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Palestinians planning violence.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Palestinians planning violence.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that "senior elements" among the Palestinians had long been laying the ground for a wave of violence without connection to his government's decision to give more benefits to Jewish settlements in occupied West Bank.
Netanyahu dismissed world criticism of Friday's decision which Washington described as troubling and the Palestinian Authority said would lead the region to an explosion.

"There is clear information that the Palestinian side, senior elements on the Palestinian side, have been planning, without connection to the government decision, for weeks, planning another wave of violence," he told Israel Radio.

Netanyahu, asked about reports Israeli Shin Bet secret service head Ami Ayalon had warned him that expansion of settlement on occupied Arab lands at this stage would cause an explosion in the areas, dismissed the reported warnings.
"Again, an inaccurate quote from inside a meeting and I do not want to enter into details now. Every security source can estimate freely, give his opinion, and that's what is done," he said.
"It is also their obligation, in my opinion, and they also understand this, that during the taking of decisions themselves that has to remain with the political echelon."

The Israeli government on Friday decided to reinstate financial benefits to settlements in the West Bank after a guerrilla attack in which a settler and her son were killed. Israel's former government that concluded interim peace deals with the Palestinians had cancelled the benefits.

"We've seen the statement and frankly it's troubling," U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said of the Israeli decision. "As I said before many times, settlement activity is unhelpful and...clearly complicates the peace process."

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's cabinet blasted the decision as destroying the peace process. "The Palestinian leadership calls on the masses everywhere to firmly confront with all possible means the Israeli settlement aggression in order to defend the land," it said in a statement.

Netanyahu's opening of an entrance to a tourist tunnel near Moslem sites in Jerusalem in September spurred clashes in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed. The media afterward said security chiefs had warned the move would spark clashes.

Dismissing world criticism of last week's decision, Netanyahu emphasised it was not simply a salve to the more than 130,000 Jewish settlers living amidst some two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
"We stand behind this decision. It is not a declarative decision. It is a decision the goal of which is to aid them both morally and materially in a series of things," he said.

The Israeli leader, who took office in June after ousting the previous centre-left government in May elections, said he called U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk on Thursday before his cabinet took the decision on Friday.

"I did call the U.S. ambassador on the eve of the decision and told him that (we)...would bring such a decision the next day to the government, that that declaration did not include the establishment of new settlements," Netanyahu said.

"In my opinion this is not the time to decide on that, perhaps it is fitting to leave a discussion on that issue to the permanent agreement when we will know exactly what are the areas of security and settlement of Israel."
